Roof typebarrel vault
    
      
      Why Owner adoption: Currey's 1912 retrospective bird's-eye labels the magazine (8) under a rounded vault, consistent with Whistler's 1808 arched front. Adopt that roof shape for the first-fort 1812 phase only. These sources give no vault radius, rise, thickness, colour or construction date. The contemporary surveyed seat, bearing and front width remain unchanged; neither the retrospective picture nor its diagnostic camera supplies a metric fit.

        Whistler, Captain John. "Fort Dearborn" [draught of the garrison and its vicinity], dated in the parade 'January 25th 1808', with its 'Index annexed to the Draught of Fort Dearborn &c.' signed at Fort Dearborn 20 February 1808. Original in the files of the War Department, Washington. Reproduced as the plate 'Fort Dearborn and Vicinity in 1808. From the original draft by Captain Whistler in the archives of the War Department at Washington', facing p. 164 of Quaife, Chicago and the Old Northwest, 1673-1835 (Chicago, 1913); the index is printed in full in note 413 on the same pages.
       source · archived
      'Bird’s-Eye View of Old Fort Dearborn.' Illustration at p. 27 of J. Seymour Currey, The Story of Old Fort Dearborn (Chicago: A. C. McClurg & Co., 1912). Numbered reconstruction of the first fort, not a contemporary view.

riseState.text:
Barrel rise (m)1.0286254881847008
    
      
      Why Not a measured vault rise. Preserve the former reconstructed gable peak: half of the shorter unchanged 3.05 m plan span times tan(34 degrees) = 1.02862548818 m above the unchanged 2.6 m wall. The old 34-degree gable parameter is no longer a visitor-facing pitch claim: a curved roof has varying tangent. A circular segment across the unchanged 4.51 m front, the existing 0.30 m projection and 0.07 m covering edge are working reconstructions, not dimensions read from Whistler or Currey. Covering, material and colour remain the existing reconstruction; the black-and-white illustration attests none of them.
      No source is named for this one.
